
Various Poisson distributions are shown in the visualisation below, for different values of\ $\lambda$.



```{r, PoissonDemo, echo=FALSE, fig.align="center", fig.cap="Poisson distributions."}
library(plotly)
library(tweedie)

# --- Parameters ---
lambdas <- c(0.5, 2)       # Two lambda values for left/right grids
alphas  <- c(1, 2)         # Gamma shape
betas   <- c(1, 2)         # Gamma scale

x_vals <- seq(0, 15, length.out = 500)  # x-axis for density

fig <- plot_ly(width = 1200, height = 600)

trace_idx <- 1
trace_map <- list(lambda0 = numeric(0), lambda2 = numeric(0))  

# --- Generate all traces ---
for(LAMBDA in lambdas){
  for(ALPHA in alphas){
    for(BETA in betas){
      
      # Map lambda, alpha, beta -> Tweedie parameters
      mu <- LAMBDA * ALPHA * BETA           # mean of compound distribution
      phi <- BETA                            # dispersion approximation
      p <- 1.5                               # compound Poisson-Gamma corresponds to 1<p<2
      # note: dtweedie returns density scaled for continuous part; point mass at zero separately
      
      # Continuous density
      dens_vals <- dtweedie(x_vals, mu=mu, phi=phi, power=p)
      
      # Probability mass at zero
      p0 <- exp(-LAMBDA)
      
      # Add zero mass marker
      fig <- fig %>% add_trace(
        x=0, y=p0,
        type="scatter", mode="markers",
        marker=list(size=10, color="red"),
        visible=(trace_idx==1),
        name=paste0("λ=", LAMBDA, ", α=", ALPHA, ", β=", BETA)
      )
      
      # Add continuous density
      fig <- fig %>% add_trace(
        x=x_vals, y=dens_vals,
        type="scatter", mode="lines",
        line=list(width=2),
        visible=(trace_idx==1),
        showlegend=FALSE
      )
      
      # Store trace indices for buttons
      if(LAMBDA == 0.5) trace_map$lambda0 <- c(trace_map$lambda0, trace_idx, trace_idx+1)
      if(LAMBDA == 2)   trace_map$lambda2 <- c(trace_map$lambda2, trace_idx, trace_idx+1)
      
      trace_idx <- trace_idx + 2
    }
  }
}

# --- Build buttons ---
build_buttons <- function(trace_indices, LAMBDA){
  buttons <- list()
  idx <- 1
  for(ALPHA in alphas){
    for(BETA in betas){
      vis <- rep(FALSE, trace_idx-1)
      vis[trace_indices[idx:(idx+1)]] <- TRUE
      buttons[[length(buttons)+1]] <- list(
        method="update",
        args=list(
          list(visible=vis),
          list(title=paste0("Compound Poisson-Gamma: λ=", LAMBDA,
                            ", α=", ALPHA, ", β=", BETA))
        ),
        label=paste0("α=", ALPHA, ", β=", BETA)
      )
      idx <- idx + 2
    }
  }
  return(buttons)
}

buttons_lambda0 <- build_buttons(trace_map$lambda0, LAMBDA=0.5)
buttons_lambda2 <- build_buttons(trace_map$lambda2, LAMBDA=2)

# --- Layout with two vertical button grids outside plot ---
fig <- fig %>% layout(
  title="Compound Poisson-Gamma Distribution (Tweedie Approx.)",
  xaxis=list(title="x", range=c(0,15)),
  yaxis=list(title="Density / P(X=0)"),
  updatemenus=list(
    # left vertical buttons
    list(type="buttons", direction="down",
         x=-0.05, y=1, xanchor="left", yanchor="top", buttons=buttons_lambda0),
    # right vertical buttons
    list(type="buttons", direction="down",
         x=1.05, y=1, xanchor="right", yanchor="top", buttons=buttons_lambda2)
  )
)

fig
```
